title: EF Core with Azure SQL
description: Connect EF Core to Azure SQL Database and apply migrations in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: EF Core works with Azure SQL Database using the same `UseSqlServer` provider as on-premises SQL Server. The main differences are connection security, retry behavior, and migration workflows in a managed environment.

data.title: Use Azure SQL with EF Core in Program.cs
data.content: Pull the connection string from configuration loaded by Key Vault or App Configuration.

data.text: In development, use `dotnet ef database update` to apply migrations. In production, use `context.Database.Migrate()` at startup or a deploy script.

data.title: Auto-apply migrations at startup
data.content: Apply pending migrations automatically when the app starts.

data.title: Production migrations
data.text: Auto-migration at startup is convenient but can fail under concurrent instances. For production, use a controlled deployment step or the `dotnet ef` CLI in your pipeline.

data.title: Build a posts API with EF Core and Azure SQL
data.description: Create a minimal API that stores posts in Azure SQL using EF Core.
steps: Add a connection string from Key Vault or local settings
Create the initial migration with `dotnet ef migrations add Initial`
Apply the migration and test CRUD endpoints
data.expectedOutcome: You can create and list posts through HTTP endpoints backed by Azure SQL.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Enable retry policies for transient Azure SQL failures
Store connection strings in Key Vault or App Configuration
Use `Migrate()` in development; prefer controlled migrations in production
data.takeaway: Azure SQL and EF Core integrate cleanly when you separate connection configuration, retry behavior, and migration strategy.
